# Standalone init outside a repository: the base becomes a git repository of
# its own, with the standard tree and the mode written explicitly.
#
# The identity reaches git through GIT_CONFIG_* environment entries, which
# outrank the machine's system and global configuration, so the scenario reads
# no identity from the host it runs on.

env GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2
env GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=user.name
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=ambient
env GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=user.email
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=ambient@local

exec akb init stand-kb
stdout '^Initialized KB "stand-kb" at .*/stand-kb$'
stdout '^commit identity: from git config \(ambient <ambient@local>\) — not recorded; each machine''s git identity applies$'

# The standard tree, plus the base's own ignore file.
exists stand-kb/.git
exists stand-kb/kb/index.md
exists stand-kb/kb/log.md
exists stand-kb/raw/files.log
exists stand-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
exists stand-kb/.agent-kb/.gitignore
exists stand-kb/.gitignore

# The config names the mode explicitly and records no identity: the ambient
# identity belongs to the machine, not to the base.
grep '^name: stand-kb$' stand-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
grep '^versioning: git$' stand-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
! grep 'git-author' stand-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
! grep 'git-email' stand-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml

cd stand-kb

# The init commit is the repository's root commit and commits under the
# machine's identity.
exec git log -1 --format=%s
stdout '^akb: init stand-kb$'
exec git log -1 --format='%an <%ae>'
stdout '^ambient <ambient@local>$'

# init writes no repository configuration of its own.
! exec git config --local user.name
! exec git config --local user.email

exec akb status
stdout '^Name: stand-kb$'
stdout '^Git: clean$'
